row.prior_work: Order inside one prompt is known to move model outputs: Chen, Chi, Wang and Zhou 2024 (ICML, arXiv:2402.08939) found permuting premise order drops reasoning accuracy by over 30%; Guan et al. 2025 (arXiv:2502.04134) found shuffled inputs lower accuracy in closed models; Hamalainen 2025 (arXiv:2504.20444; ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, versions unnamed) found list order shifts candidate ratings, model-dependently. That predicts the questions-only gate passes. No paper found compares a one-message order effect with a turn-by-turn chain on graded credences, or asks whether it spreads across items; em-gm2q (Haiku, Sonnet, 10 items, mixed, one item per model) is the only one. So parts (3)–(5) of the rule are unpredicted (predicts: unknown). Adds: Opus; 30 new items on Sonnet; no item allowed to carry it; a wrong-target check at both ends of the list. The odds (6%) sit far below "the gate passes" because the gate is one of five parts and both models must clear all five.

fields.prior_work: Kim and Kang 2026 hold verbalized answers and scores fixed and vary the context in which token probability is read; the verbalized-minus-token gap shifts (19/20 ECE, 17/20 AUROC, 95% intervals), mostly through that context's instruction text; their verbalized-wording variation is a 0–100 scale (App. B.1); stated confidence also depends on how a supplied answer is worded. Human calibration work on format dependence (half-range 'my answer is correct' against full-range 'the statement is true'; Ferrell; Juslin, Wennerholm and Olsson 1999; Winman, Hansson and Juslin 2004) names the referent mechanism in people; none tests threshold-list overlap. fields.novelty_line: **Novelty:** partly new. That a verbalized-confidence threshold flags different questions when only the prompt changes is in print: Zhao et al. (2025, arXiv:2505.21701), with a "probability that your guess is correct" prompt on open 7–8B models, find that shuffling the answer options leaves the rejected sets overlapping only .61 (Mistral-7B) and .20 (Llama-3.1-8B) on MMLU, and Kim and Kang (2026, arXiv:2605.27752; open models, no Claude) caution that a threshold set under one prompt may not hold under another. In people, calibration depends on the response format (half-range against full-range; Hansson, Juslin and Winman 2003, CogSci Proceedings). No paper found compares a probability format with an "out of 100 such questions" frequency format for model confidence, measures the flagged-set change against two askings in the same format, or fixes the number's referent to the model's own guess; ours does all three on Sonnet 5.5 (gap +0.27, unreplicated) and agrees in direction with the prompt-instability work, but cannot separate the referent fix from the switch to Yes/No answers. Search: WebSearch plus arXiv and eScholarship opens for "verbalized confidence" with "frequency format", "out of 100 similar questions", "confidence-frequency effect", "half-range full-range format dependence", "selective prediction threshold prompt instability", "answer polarity yes/no confidence", "probability that your answer is correct" referent; 2026-11-05. claude-opus-5-5.
